But by the 1 930s, the uncertainty principle dismantled this conception of reality by showing that you can't ever know both the position and the velocity of a particle; you can't ever know both the value of a field at some location in space and how quickly the field value is changing. Quantum uncertainty forbids it. As we discussed in the last chapter, this quantum uncertainty ensures that the microworld is a turbulent and jittery realm. Earlier, we focused on uncertainty-induced quantum jitters for the inflaton field, but quan tum uncertainty applies to all fields. The electromagnetic field, the strong and weak nuclear force fields, and the gravitational field are all subject to frenzied quantum jitters on microscopic scales. In fact, these field jitters exist even in space you'd normally think of as empty, space that would seem to contain no matter and no fields.
